title: agentic-foundation repository configuration (v2)
description: Schema for .agentic/config.yml — a platform-neutral contract for a graph of SDLC/STLC agent stages. Validated by the installer before rendering per-platform pipelines. Easy by default (a `profile` expands to a stage graph); granular when wanted (define `stages` explicitly). Any provider/model per stage; any SCM platform; any language. Secrets are referenced by NAME only; values never live here. See docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

extends.description: Base config(s) to inherit from, merged before this file (local values win). Layer an org base -> team base -> repo. A string or an ordered list; each item is a path or URI the installer can read.

profile.description: Onboarding shortcut. Expands to a default stage graph you can then override via `stages`. `custom` adds no stages (you define them all).

platform.description: The SCM/CI platform this repo lives on. The contract is platform-neutral; a per-platform renderer maps it to that system's pipeline. (GitHub renderer ships first.)

host.description: For self-hosted / enterprise (e.g. github.example.com, a self-managed GitLab, dev.azure.com/org). Blank = the platform's public host.

trusted_roles.description: Normalized author-permission levels allowed to drive agentic changes; the renderer maps them to the platform's own roles.

token_secret.description: NAME of the secret holding the platform API token. Never the value.

defaults.description: Org/account-level fallbacks. A stage that does not set its own provider/model resolves here; if nothing resolves the run fails loudly (there is no hidden toolkit fallback).

provider.description: Default provider id for stages that omit one.

models.description: Default model binding per provider id (open map — any provider).
Provider-agnostic model aliases. Reference an alias name anywhere a model is expected and map it per provider here, so model-ID churn touches one place.

providers.description: Per-provider connection settings, keyed by provider id (open map — claude, openai, gemini, azure_openai, bedrock, vertex, ollama, openai_compatible, custom, ...). Endpoint/version/deployment plus the NAME of the key secret. Lets you point at self-hosted / cloud / proxy / on-prem gateways. Never a secret value.

skills.description: Skill registry, keyed by skill id. A skill is the reusable methodology/content for a stage (checklist, rubric, output format) — provider-, backend-, and language-agnostic. Register your own or override a shipped one by id. Built-ins live in templates/skills/<id>/. Referenced from stages via `stages[].skill`.

stages.description: The agent pipeline as an ordered, extensible graph. Each stage is one agent bound to a provider+model and a backend. Merged onto the `profile`'s stages (a stage here with the same id overrides the profile's).

tiering.description: Global deterministic model tiering (change size + paths -> trivial/standard/complex), reused with no extra model call. A stage may opt out with `tiering: false`.

guardrails.description: Prompt-injection / untrusted-input controls. Content from PRs/MRs, issues, comments, and diffs is treated as data, not instructions.

observability.description: Where run records go. Adapts to your stack — file, CI artifact, webhook, or OTLP collector — with endpoints supplied by variable/secret NAME, never hardcoded. Secrets are always redacted from output.

build.description: What "green" means for THIS repository. Optional: omit it for a repo with no build gate (e.g. docs-only). Language-agnostic — stages run exactly what is set here and assume no language.

stage.description: One agent in the pipeline. `id` is always required; `type` is required unless `from` supplies it via an agent preset. Provider/model resolve through the precedence chain; the backend defaults to the generic runner.

id.description: Unique stage id, e.g. plan, implement, security, integration-test.

type.description: Semantic role; drives sensible defaults (e.g. review/security/test default to a blocking gate; plan/docs to advisory).

from.description: Agent-preset id to base this stage on (from templates/agents/). Fields set here override the preset.

provider.description: Provider id for this stage. Omit to inherit defaults.provider.

skill.description: Skill id (from `skills` registry or a built-in) supplying this stage's methodology. Takes precedence over inline `instructions`.

gate.description: advisory = comment only; blocking = emits a required status check. Omit to use the type's default.

depends_on.description: Ids of stages that must run before this one (defines the graph).

instructions.description: Inline prompt/policy for the stage, or a path to a prompt file.

backend.description: The executor for a stage. `generic` is the built-in prompt-runner; the named adapters wrap mature OSS agents. `with` carries backend-specific inputs; `uses` overrides the action/image for `custom`.

uses.description: Action ref or container image (for `custom`, or to pin/override an adapter).

with.description: Backend-specific inputs passed through to the executor.

budgets.description: Cost / token ceilings. All limits are opt-in; set only what you want enforced. Usable globally or per-stage.

modelBinding.description: Optional model binding. Every field is optional so a caller can override only what they need (e.g. just the `complex` tier). A value may be a literal model ID or an alias name from `models.aliases`.

skillRef.description: A registry entry pointing at a skill's content. `builtin` uses templates/skills/<id>/; `path`/`uri` load your own; `extends` layers this skill on top of another (base first, this overrides).

extends.description: Base skill id this one extends.

modelAlias.description: One alias mapped to a concrete model ID per provider id (open map).

providerConn.description: Provider connection settings. Contains NO secret values — only the name of the secret to read.

observabilitySink.description: A single destination for run records. `endpoint_var`/`headers_secret` are NAMES of a variable/secret, so the actual URL and token stay out of config.
